extractions.value: Prednisone 10 mg/day started July 1994, increased to 60 mg/day March 1996, tapered to 10 mg/day May 1996; Plasmapheresis three times per week March 1996, reduced to twice per week, then once per week; MMF 2 g/day; IVIG 0.5 g/kg once per week; Cyclophosphamide 1700 mg IV after three plasmaphereses 11 Sep 1996, then oral 50 mg/day for 2 weeks.
extractions.quote: Prednisone had already been started at 10 mg/day in July 1994 to treat a severe insulin resistance. Due to a limited response to high-dose diazepam (240 mg/day) plasmapheresis began in March 1996 and was performed three times per week, MMF was given at 2 g/day, and prednisone was increased to 60 mg/day in addition to diazepam and baclofen. Due to her increased mobility, plasmapheresis was reduced to twice per week and prednisone tapered to 10 mg/day by May 1996. In order to further decrease GAD65 autoantibody levels as well as the frequency of plasmapheresis to improve quality of life, she received IVIG at the dose of 0.5 g/kg once per week while continuing other therapies in late June 1996. MMF was discontinued and a trial of cyclophosphamide began in September 1996 (Fig. 2 D). Following a protocol similar to that for treating systemic lupus erythematosus with plasmaphereis, she received an intravenous infusion of 1700 mg cyclophosphamide after three consecutive plasmaphereses on 11 September 1996. Plasmapheresis was then stopped for 3 weeks. Due to the development of neutropenia, oral cyclophosphamide (50 mg/day) was not begun until 27 September 1996. She was then treated with oral cyclophosphamide for 2 weeks. Restarting plasmapheresis (2/weeks) again gradually decreased GAD65 autoantibody levels. The plasmapheresis was then decreased to once per week, which has continued through the present time. The patient continued to receive plasmapheresis (1/week), intrathecal baclofen and diazepam 5 mg/day with stabilization of stiffness and muscular pain.
